items.reason: Needs network: all 25 refs are first-party actions/* on 4 distinct tags (checkout@v7, setup-node@v6, upload-artifact@v7, download-artifact@v7) and pinning means asking GitHub what each tag points at today; scripts/actions-pin.mjs --update already resolves them AND flips STRICT/RATCHET in the same pass, so the close is one networked command, not new code.

Needs a build: a page-weight budget is only a gate once it carries a measured ceiling, and there is no node_modules and no .next in this worktree, so today's number for / and /app cannot be produced — a budget file written without one would be a ceiling nobody measured.

Needs a test runner: a mutation score over src/lib/llm/ and the store seams is a measurement, and without the ability to run node --test there is no survival rate to record and no honest threshold to gate on.

Needs shell: the drill has to be RUN to leave a timing, and the Results table is still empty; the runbook, the ranked detection layers and the seeds are now written so the first run is a bounded 30-minute execution rather than a design task.

lessons: This repository already answers most maturity questions with a zero-dependency node script plus a committed baseline, and ADR-0007 forbids adding a check that cannot pass today — so any new gate here is blocked on producing its first measurement, which is precisely what a no-shell session cannot do. Recognising that early is worth more than shipping an unrunnable script.

Before adding an ADR here, check docs/adr/: adr-check.mjs treats a record with 3+ higher-numbered successors as settled and then REQUIRES a '## Consequences observed' section, so a new ADR can retroactively fail the gate on an older one.

The repo's own gates already answer questions a recovery plan would otherwise re-derive: 'Revert "..."' is exempt from the commit-subject rule (scripts/commit-subject.mjs EXEMPT), and .agent/checkpoints/*.json without an 'endedAt' field is an existing, committed marker for stopped-session commits — no new trailer is needed to find them.
